'''Leroy''' "'''Lee'''" '''Cronin''' <small>[[Fellowship of the Royal Society of Edinburgh|FRSE]] [[Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]]</small> (born 1 June 1973)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chem.gla.ac.uk/cronin/biography.php |title=The Cronin Group |access-date=2011-09-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110924185756/http://www.chem.gla.ac.uk/cronin/biography.php |archive-date=24 September 2011 }} Cronin CV</ref> is the [[Regius Professor of Chemistry (Glasgow)|Regius Chair of Chemistry]] in the School of Chemistry at the [[University of Glasgow]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Prof Leroy Cronin|url=http://www.gla.ac.uk/stafflist/?action=person&id=4fdceee18a90203c98f3|publisher=[[University of Glasgow]]|access-date=20 February 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gla.ac.uk:443/newsreview/story.cfm?id=215|title=University of Glasgow News Review: Tiny molecule is 10,000 times thinner than a single hair|website=Gla.ac.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/scotland/4573117.stm|title=Chips squeezed by nanoscale work|date=23 May 2005|access-date=31 October 2021|website=News.bbc.co.uk}}</ref> He was elected to the Fellowship of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]], the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]], and appointed to the Regius Chair of Chemistry in 2013. He was previously the Gardiner Chair, appointed April 2009.

==Biography==
Cronin was awarded BSc (1994) and PhD (1997) from the [[University of York]]. From 1997 to 1999, he was a [[Leverhulme]] fellow at the [[University of Edinburgh]] working with Neil Robertson. From 1999 to 2000 he worked as an [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Alexander von Humboldt]] research fellow in the laboratory of [[Achim Mueller]] at the [[University of Bielefeld]] (1999–2000). In 2000, he joined the [[University of Birmingham]] as a lecturer in chemistry, and in 2002 he moved to a similar position at the University of Glasgow. In 2005, he was promoted to Reader at the [[University of Glasgow]], EPSRC Advanced Fellow followed by promotion to Professor of Chemistry in 2006, and in 2009 became the Gardiner Professor. In 2013, he became the [[Regius Professor of Chemistry (Glasgow)]].{{citation needed|date=December 2024}}

In 2012 Cronin was described to be designing<ref>{{cite news |title=Chemputer that prints out drugs |newspaper=The Observer |date=21 July 2012 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2012/jul/21/chemputer-that-prints-out-drugs |last1=Adams |first1=Tim }}</ref> robots using 3D printed-architectures<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Symes |first1=Mark D. |last2=Kitson |first2=Philip J. |last3=Yan |first3=Jun |last4=Richmond |first4=Craig J. |last5=Cooper |first5=Geoffrey J. Hessam M. |last2=Craven |first2=Matthew |last3=Leonov |first3=Artem I. |last4=Keenan |first4=Graham |last5=Cronin |first5=Leroy |title=A universal system for digitization and automatic execution of the chemical synthesis literature |journal=Science |date=2 October 2020 |volume=370 |issue=6512 |pages=101–108 |doi=10.1126/science.abc2986 |pmid=33004517 |bibcode=2020Sci...370..101M |url=https://eprints.gla.ac.uk/221626/1/221626.pdf }}{{primary source inline|date=September 2024}}</ref> and this was demonstrated by reading the chemistry synthesis literature and converting it into executable chemical code.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rohrbach |first1=Simon |last2=Šiaučiulis |first2=Mindaugas |last3=Chisholm |first3=Greig |last4=Pirvan |first4=Petrisor-Alin |last5=Saleeb |first5=Michael |last6=Mehr |first6=S. Hessam M. |last7=Trushina |first7=Ekaterina |last8=Leonov |first8=Artem I. |last9=Keenan |first9=Graham |last10=Khan |first10=Aamir |last11=Hammer |first11=Alexander |last12=Cronin |first12=Leroy |title=Digitization and validation of a chemical synthesis literature database in the ChemPU |journal=Science |date=8 July 2022 |volume=377 |issue=6602 |pages=172–180 |doi=10.1126/science.abo0058 |pmid=35857541 |bibcode=2022Sci...377..172R }}{{page needed|date=September 2024}}</ref> A spinoff company led by Cronin, called '''Chemify''', was launched in 2019 and raised £33m in 2023.<ref>{{cite news |title=Glasgow firm Chemify raises £33m to 'digitise' chemistry |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-scotland-business-66376431 |access-date=18 December 2024 |work=BBC News |date=1 August 2023}}</ref>

In 2017 Cronin first published the concept of [[assembly theory]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Marshall |first1=Stuart M. |last2=Murray |first2=Alastair R. G. |last3=Cronin |first3=Leroy |title=A probabilistic framework for identifying biosignatures using Pathway Complexity |journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences |date=28 December 2017 |volume=375 |issue=2109 |article-number=20160342 |doi=10.1098/rsta.2016.0342 |pmid=29133442 |pmc=5686400 |arxiv=1705.03460 |bibcode=2017RSPTA.37560342M }}{{primary source inline|date=September 2024}}</ref> which aims to quantify how complex a molecule is, considering how many steps it would take to build the molecule using the minimum number of steps to add together the various parts allowing reuse.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Marshall |first1=Stuart M. |last2=Mathis |first2=Cole |last3=Carrick |first3=Emma |last4=Keenan |first4=Graham |last5=Cooper |first5=Geoffrey J. T. |last6=Graham |first6=Heather |last7=Craven |first7=Matthew |last8=Gromski |first8=Piotr S. |last9=Moore |first9=Douglas G. |last10=Walker |first10=Sara. I. |last11=Cronin |first11=Leroy |title=Identifying molecules as biosignatures with assembly theory and mass spectrometry |journal=Nature Communications |date=24 May 2021 |volume=12 |issue=1 |page=3033 |doi=10.1038/s41467-021-23258-x  |doi-access=free|pmid=34031398 |pmc=8144626 |bibcode=2021NatCo..12.3033M }}{{primary source inline|date=September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Ball |first=Philip |date=4 May 2023 |title=A New Theory for the Assembly of Life in the Universe |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/a-new-theory-for-the-assembly-of-life-in-the-universe-20230504/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Zimmer |first=Carl |date=2024-07-31 |title=A Test for Life Versus Non-Life |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/07/31/science/assembly-theory-life-sara-walker.html |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Walker |first=Sara Imari |title=Life As No One Knows It: The Physics of Life's Emergence |date=2024 |publisher=Penguin Publishing Group |isbn=978-0-593-19189-7 |location=New York}}</ref>

In 2022 Cronin was suspended by the Royal Society of Chemistry for three months for breaching their code of conduct, following an investigation of a complaint made by a third party.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Holden |first1=John-Paul |title=Top scientist suspended from Royal Society of Chemistry |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/business_hq/20283583.professor-lee-cronin-suspended-royal-society-chemistry/ |access-date=16 July 2022 |publisher= [[The Herald (Glasgow)|The Herald]] |date=16 July 2022 |language=en|quote=A Glasgow University spokesman said: "The university is aware that Professor Lee Cronin has had his membership of the Royal Society of Chemistry suspended for a three-month period, following a full independent investigation into a complaint made by a third party."}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| last=Inge |first=Sophie|url=https://www.researchprofessionalnews.com/rr-news-uk-charities-and-societies-2022-7-top-chemist-suspended-by-royal-society-of-chemistry/|title=Top chemist suspended by Royal Society of Chemistry|work=Research Professional News|date=15 July 2022|access-date=25 July 2022| quote=Lee Cronin (pictured), the University of Glasgow's Regius chair of chemistry, was suspended for three months by the society, following a complaint, the RSC announced in Update, its monthly newsletter for members.}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==

* 2007 [[Philip Leverhulme Prize]] by the Leverhulme Trust<ref>{{cite web |title=Philip Leverhulme Prize Prizes |url=https://docs.google.com/viewer?url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.leverhulme.ac.uk%2Ffiles%2Fseealsodocs%2F341%2F2007.PDF |access-date=2012-07-28 |publisher=Leverhulme Trust}}</ref>
* 2012 Royal Society of Chemistry [[Corday–Morgan medal]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Corday–Morgan Prizes |url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/CordayMorganPrizes/ |access-date=2012-06-20 |publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry}}</ref>
* 2014 recognised as one of the UK's top 10 Inspiring Scientists and Engineers (RISE)<ref>{{cite web |title=Leroy (Lee) Cronin - EPSRC website |url=https://www.epsrc.ac.uk/about/people/leroycronin/ |website=Epsrc.ac.uk|date=3 October 2024 }}</ref> as well as being recognised as one of the top 100 UK practising Scientists by the UK Science Council.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 list of leading UK practising scientists |url=http://www.sciencecouncil.org/content/2014-list-leading-uk-practising-scientists%20 |access-date=31 October 2021 |publisher=The Science Council}}</ref>
* 2015 Royal Society of Edinburgh BP / Hutton Prize for Energy innovation.<ref>{{cite web |title=Home - The Royal Society of Edinburgh |url=https://rse.org.uk/resources/resource/video/removing-fossil-fuel/ |website=The Royal Society of Edinburgh|date=3 June 2021 }}</ref> Royal Society of Chemistry [[Tilden Prize]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Tilden Prize |url=https://www.rsc.org/prizes-funding/prizes/find-a-prize/tilden-prizes/previous-winners/ |access-date=March 5, 2023 |publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry}}</ref>
* 2018 American Chemical Society Inorganic Chemistry Lectureship<ref>{{Cite web |last=Howell |first=Brooke |title=Lee Cronin Wins 2018 Inorganic Chemistry Lectureship |url=https://axial.acs.org/2018/03/15/inorganic-chemistry-lectureship/ |website=ACS Axial|date=15 March 2018}}</ref> [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] Interdisciplinary Prize for his work developing the field of digital chemistry
